rv.q: Lauryn Ajufo’s magnetic and irrepressible performance makes Michaela Coel’s darkly comic monologue completely her own
It is intelligent, inventive and still arresting.
This revival of her debut, with a poignant sound design from Xana and clever lighting from Christopher Nairne, cements Cole’s play as a modern classic.
Ajufo is a firecracker on stage.

Standing once as a beacon of what was to come for Michaela Coel, the show now stands as proof of her undeniable legacy, as well as a breathtaking showcase for another up-and-comer in Lauryn Ajufo's finely-tuned performance.
His production, with partner company Tiata Fahodzi, is a really invigorating experience.

cn.t: Michaela Coel's 2012 debut monologue proves timeless in its first revival, with Lauryn Ajufo's magnetic performance making the role her own. Critics praise the darkly comic one-woman show's continued relevance and emotional punch.
